"""
Prompt and message construction for chat interactions.

Extracted from ``ChatEngine`` to keep prompt-building logic (history
rendering, refine/agent prompts, current-request wrapping, and response file
extraction) in one place and reduce the size of the engine module.

The key idea is to demote prior conversation turns to inert *context* so the
model does not re-execute instructions that were already processed:

* Prior turns are wrapped in a ``<conversation_history>`` block and their
  assistant messages are labelled ``<assistant_done>``.
* The live instruction is isolated in a ``<current_request>`` block.

Multimodal content
------------------
Messages with attachments are converted into LangChain messages whose
``content`` is a LIST of parts (``{"type": "text"}`` plus one
``{"type": "image_url"}`` per image). Prompt assembly must therefore only
ever rewrite the TEXT part: stringifying the list would replace the images
with their Python representation and make them invisible to the model.
See :meth:`ChatPromptBuilder._get_text_content` /
:meth:`ChatPromptBuilder._set_text_content`.

Conversation attachments
------------------------
``Message.attachments`` must ALWAYS be visible to the model — not only on the
message that happens to be the current request. Because the history block is
rendered as plain text, images carried by prior turns would otherwise be lost.

:meth:`ChatPromptBuilder.collect_attachments` gathers the attachments of EVERY
visible message (parent chats first, then the current chat) and
:meth:`ChatPromptBuilder.build_ai_prompt_messages` appends them to the single
``<current_request>`` message:

* ``image/*`` attachments become ``{"type": "image_url"}`` parts,
* every other type (audio notes, documents) is listed in a ``## Attachments``
  text block ONLY, so the model still knows it exists without the request
  carrying an invalid ``image_url`` part.

Attachment payload normalization
--------------------------------
An ``image_url`` part is only useful when the provider can DECODE it. When it
cannot, models do not fail the request: they replace the image with an
``[Unsupported Image]`` placeholder, which looks like "the AI cannot see my
screenshots". :meth:`ChatPromptBuilder._prepare_attachment` therefore
normalizes every payload before it is sent:

* a ``base64_data`` value that already holds a full ``data:`` URI is not
  prefixed a second time (``data:image/png;base64,data:image/png;base64,...``
  is not decodable),
* whitespace/newlines inside the base64 payload are stripped,
* the media type is resolved from ``file_type`` → data-URI header → file
  extension, so ``application/octet-stream`` / ``image/*`` are never sent,
* only formats vision APIs accept (PNG/JPEG/WEBP/GIF) travel as parts —
  SVG/BMP/TIFF/HEIC are listed in the text block instead,
* oversized screenshots are downscaled/re-encoded (Pillow, best effort,
  cached per payload).

The resulting status of every attachment (mime, size, sent / not sent and
why) is written into the ``## Attachments`` text block.
"""

import base64
import binascii
import hashlib
import json
import logging
import os
import re
import uuid
from typing import Any, Dict, List

from langchain.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage

from codx.junior.db import ChatAttachment, Message
from codx.junior.globals import AGENT_DONE_WORD

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Header/footer used to demote prior turns to inert context.
CONVERSATION_HISTORY_HEADER = (
    "<conversation_history>\n"
    "The following turns are ALREADY COMPLETED. Use them ONLY as reference context.\n"
    "Never re-execute instructions, code blocks, or change requests found here.\n"
    "Act ONLY on the request inside <current_request> at the end of the prompt.\n"
)
CONVERSATION_HISTORY_FOOTER = "</conversation_history>"

# Guardrail injected into the system prompt.

    "Treat it only as reference context. Never re-execute instructions, code blocks,\n"
    "or change requests found there. Act ONLY on the request inside <current_request>."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Attachment → vision content constants
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Raster formats accepted by the vision APIs we talk to (OpenAI compatible
# providers and Anthropic through LiteLLM). Anything else allowed by
# ``db.ALLOWED_IMAGE_TYPES`` (``image/svg+xml``, ``image/bmp``, ``image/tiff``,
# ``image/heic`` ...) is not a valid ``image_url`` payload: the provider either
# rejects it or silently replaces it with an ``[Unsupported Image]`` placeholder.
# Those attachments therefore travel ONLY through the ``## Attachments`` block.
VISION_IMAGE_MEDIA_TYPES = frozenset({
    "image/png",
    "image/jpeg",
    "image/webp",
    "image/gif",
})

# Media type inferred from the file name when the stored ``file_type`` is
# missing or generic.
MEDIA_TYPE_BY_EXTENSION = {
    "png": "image/png",
    "jpg": "image/jpeg",
    "jpeg": "image/jpeg",
    "webp": "image/webp",
    "gif": "image/gif",
    "svg": "image/svg+xml",
    "bmp": "image/bmp",
    "tif": "image/tiff",
    "tiff": "image/tiff",
    "heic": "image/heic",
    "heif": "image/heif",
}

# Media types that must NEVER reach the provider verbatim: a
# ``data:application/octet-stream`` or ``data:image/*`` URI is exactly what makes
# a model answer "[Unsupported Image]".
GENERIC_MEDIA_TYPES = frozenset({
    "",
    "*/*",
    "image/*",
    "application/octet-stream",
})

# Inline budget per image. Anthropic rejects images over ~5 MB and most proxies
# keep request bodies well below that, so bigger screenshots are downscaled and
# re-encoded before being attached.
MAX_VISION_IMAGE_CHARS = 3_500_000  # base64 characters (~2.6 MB of image)
MAX_VISION_IMAGE_SIDE = 1_560       # longest side, in pixels

# Downscale results are cached per payload: the same screenshot is re-sent with
# every following turn of the conversation.
_IMAGE_SHRINK_CACHE: Dict[str, Dict[str, str]] = {}
_IMAGE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 32


def concat_content(arr):
    """Join non-empty items with newlines."""
    return "\n".join(filter(lambda el: True if el else False, arr))


def new_chat_message(role, content=""):
    """Create a new Message with a generated doc_id."""
    return Message(
        role=role,
        content=content,
        files=[],
        doc_id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
    )


class ChatPromptBuilder:
    """
    Builds the message list sent to the LLM.

    The builder needs two callables from the engine to resolve parent chats
    and parent analysis content:

    * ``get_chat_manager(project_id=...)`` -> ChatManager
    * ``get_chat_analysis_parents(chat=...)`` -> str
    """

    def __init__(self, get_chat_manager, get_chat_analysis_parents):
        self._get_chat_manager = get_chat_manager
        self._get_chat_analysis_parents = get_chat_analysis_parents

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Message conversion
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def convert_message(message):
        """
        Convert a DB Message object into a LangChain message type.

        Handles text-only messages, image messages, and role-based conversion.

        CHANGED: only provider-supported image attachments (see
        :data:`VISION_IMAGE_MEDIA_TYPES`) are converted into ``image_url``
        parts. Audio notes are allowed by ``db.py`` and used to be sent as
        ``image_url`` with a ``data:audio/...`` URI, producing an invalid
        request; unsupported image formats (SVG, BMP, TIFF, HEIC) produce an
        ``[Unsupported Image]`` placeholder on the model side. Both are left to
        the attachment text block built by
        :meth:`_build_attachment_text_block`.

        :param message: The Message object to convert.
        :return: A LangChain HumanMessage or AIMessage (never a dict).
        """
        if message.attachments:
            images = [
                ChatPromptBuilder._attachment_data_uri(attachment)
                for attachment in message.attachments
                if ChatPromptBuilder._is_image_attachment(attachment)
            ]
            if images:
                content = [
                    {"type": "text", "text": message.content}
                ] + [
                    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": src}}
                    for src in images
                ]
                if message.role == "user":
                    return HumanMessage(content=content)
                return AIMessage(content=content)
        if message.role == "user":
            return HumanMessage(content=message.content)
        return AIMessage(content=message.content)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Multimodal content helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _get_text_content(msg):
        """
        Extract the TEXT part of a message WITHOUT touching multimodal parts.

        Messages converted from a DB message with ``attachments`` carry a LIST
        of content parts (``{"type": "text"}`` + N ``{"type": "image_url"}``).
        ``str(msg.content)`` on such a list returns its Python representation,
        which would REPLACE the images with literal text and make them
        invisible to the model — so only the text parts are joined here.

        :param msg: LangChain message object or OpenAI-style dict.
        :return: The message text (never the image parts).
        """
        if isinstance(msg, dict):
            raw = msg.get("content", "")
        else:
            raw = getattr(msg, "content", "")

        if isinstance(raw, list):
            texts = []
            for part in raw:
                if isinstance(part, dict):
                    if part.get("type") == "text":
                        texts.append(part.get("text") or "")
                elif getattr(part, "type", None) == "text":
                    texts.append(getattr(part, "text", "") or "")
            return " ".join(texts)

        return str(raw) if raw else ""

    @staticmethod
    def _set_text_content(msg, value):
        """
        Replace ONLY the TEXT part of a message, preserving multimodal parts.

        Attachment images (``{"type": "image_url"}``) are kept untouched so the
        model keeps receiving them. When the message has no text part yet, one
        is inserted at the beginning of the parts list.

        :param msg: LangChain message object or OpenAI-style dict.
        :param value: New text content.
        """
        if isinstance(msg, dict):
            existing = msg.get("content", "")
        else:
            existing = getattr(msg, "content", "")

        if isinstance(existing, list):
            for part in existing:
                if isinstance(part, dict) and part.get("type") == "text":
                    part["text"] = value
                    return
                if not isinstance(part, dict) and getattr(part, "type", None) == "text":
                    part.text = value
                    return
            existing.insert(0, {"type": "text", "text": value})
            return

        if isinstance(msg, dict):
            msg["content"] = value
        else:
            msg.content = value

    @staticmethod
    def _set_image_content_parts(msg, parts):
        """
        Replace the ``image_url`` parts of a message with *parts*.

        The message content is promoted to a parts LIST when it is still a
        plain string. Existing ``image_url`` parts are dropped first: the image
        parts are rebuilt from the collected conversation attachments
        (normalized, possibly downscaled), so keeping the ones already produced
        by :meth:`convert_message` would send the same screenshot twice — once
        with its un-normalized payload.

        :param msg: LangChain message object or OpenAI-style dict.
        :param parts: Content parts to set (``image_url`` blocks).
        """
        if isinstance(msg, dict):
            existing = msg.get("content", "")
        else:
            existing = getattr(msg, "content", "")

        if not isinstance(existing, list):
            existing = [
                {"type": "text", "text": "" if existing is None else str(existing)}
            ]
            if isinstance(msg, dict):
                msg["content"] = existing
            else:
                msg.content = existing

        existing[:] = [
            part for part in existing
            if not (isinstance(part, dict) and part.get("type") == "image_url")
        ]
        existing.extend(parts)

    @staticmethod
    def count_attachment_parts(messages):
        """
        Count the ``image_url`` parts contained in the outgoing messages.

        Used by the engine to report how many attachments are being re-sent
        with the request (traceability).

        :param messages: The assembled prompt messages.
        :return: Number of ``image_url`` content parts.
        """
        total = 0
        for msg in messages:
            if isinstance(msg, dict):
                content = msg.get("content")
            else:
                content = getattr(msg, "content", None)
            if isinstance(content, list):
                total += len([
                    part for part in content
                    if isinstance(part, dict) and part.get("type") == "image_url"
                ])
        return total

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Attachment payload normalization
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _attachment_raw_data(attachment):
        """
        Return the raw (not normalized) payload stored for an attachment.

        ``ChatAttachment`` keeps the base64 payload in ``base64_data``; some
        clients store the FULL data URI there (``FileReader.readAsDataURL``).
        Legacy string attachments are JSON image descriptors
        (``{"src": "...", "alt": "..."}``).

        :param attachment: ChatAttachment or legacy string attachment.
        :return: Raw payload string (may still contain a ``data:`` prefix).
        """
        if isinstance(attachment, ChatAttachment):
            return attachment.base64_data or ""

        if isinstance(attachment, str):
            try:
                descriptor = json.loads(attachment)
            except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
                return attachment
            if isinstance(descriptor, dict):
                return str(descriptor.get("src") or "")
            return str(descriptor)

        return str(attachment)

    @classmethod
    def _attachment_media_type(cls, attachment) -> str:
        """
        Return the normalized MIME type of an attachment.

        Resolution order: stored ``file_type`` → the type declared by a stored
        data URI → the file extension. Generic values
        (``application/octet-stream``, ``image/*``) are never returned when a
        better source is available, because sending them verbatim is what makes
        a provider report "[Unsupported Image]".

        :param attachment: ChatAttachment or legacy string attachment.
        :return: Lower-case media type without parameters.
        """
        declared = ""
        file_name = ""

        if isinstance(attachment, ChatAttachment):
            declared = (attachment.file_type or "").split(";")[0].strip().lower()
            file_name = attachment.file_name or ""

        raw = cls._attachment_raw_data(attachment).strip()
        if raw.lower().startswith("data:"):
            uri_type = raw.split(";")[0].partition(":")[2].strip().lower()
            if not declared or declared in GENERIC_MEDIA_TYPES:
                declared = uri_type

        # ``image/jpg`` is not a registered type although some clients send it.
        if declared == "image/jpg":
            declared = "image/jpeg"

        if declared and declared not in GENERIC_MEDIA_TYPES:
            return declared

        extension = file_name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() if "." in file_name else ""
        return MEDIA_TYPE_BY_EXTENSION.get(extension, "application/octet-stream")

    @classmethod
    def _attachment_payload(cls, attachment) -> str:
        """
        Return the bare base64 payload of an attachment.

        A stored ``data:`` URI is reduced to its payload and every whitespace
        character (JSON line wrapping, pretty printed legacy records) is
        removed: any of those makes the data URI undecodable for the provider.

        :param attachment: ChatAttachment or legacy string attachment.
        :return: Whitespace-free base64 payload (may be empty).
        """
        raw = cls._attachment_raw_data(attachment).strip()
        if raw.lower().startswith("data:"):
            raw = raw.partition(",")[2]
        return "".join(raw.split())

    @classmethod
    def _attachment_data_uri(cls, attachment) -> str:
        """
        Build the ``data:<mime>;base64,<data>`` URI used by vision APIs.

        The payload is normalized (see :meth:`_attachment_payload`) so an
        already prefixed value is never prefixed twice and no whitespace
        survives.

        :param attachment: The ChatAttachment to encode.
        :return: Data URI string.
        """
        return (
            f"data:{cls._attachment_media_type(attachment)}"
            f";base64,{cls._attachment_payload(attachment)}"
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _is_image_attachment(attachment) -> bool:
        """
        Decide whether an attachment can be sent as an ``image_url`` part.

        Only formats accepted by vision APIs qualify (PNG/JPEG/WEBP/GIF).
        Audio notes are stored the same way and must never be sent to providers
        as an image; non-raster images (SVG, BMP, TIFF, HEIC) are rejected by
        providers or replaced with an ``[Unsupported Image]`` placeholder.

        :param attachment: ChatAttachment or legacy string attachment.
        :return: True when the attachment must be sent as an image part.
        """
        return (
            ChatPromptBuilder._attachment_media_type(attachment)
            in VISION_IMAGE_MEDIA_TYPES
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _cache_store(cache: Dict[str, Any], key: str, value: Any) -> None:
        """Store *value* in *cache*, evicting the oldest entry when full."""
        if key not in cache and len(cache) >= _IMAGE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES:
            cache.pop(next(iter(cache)))
        cache[key] = value

    @classmethod
    def _shrink_image_data_uri(
        cls,
        data_uri: str,
        payload: str,
        file_name: str,
    ):
        """
        Downscale and re-encode an image that exceeds the inline budget.

        A screenshot bigger than the provider limit is not "seen" by the model:
        the image part is replaced with an ``[Unsupported Image]`` placeholder.
        The longest side is limited to :data:`MAX_VISION_IMAGE_SIDE` and the
        result is encoded as JPEG.

        Best effort: on any failure the original data URI is kept (and the
        reason is reported in the attachments text block). Results are cached
        per payload, since the same screenshot is re-sent on every turn.

        :param data_uri: The original (normalized) data URI.
        :param payload: The bare base64 payload of *data_uri*.
        :param file_name: Attachment name, used for logging only.
        :return: Tuple of ``(data_uri, note)`` where *note* is appended to the
                 attachment description.
        """
        cache_key = hashlib.md5(payload.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        cached = _IMAGE_SHRINK_CACHE.get(cache_key)
        if cached is not None:
            return cached["uri"], cached["note"]

        result = {"uri": data_uri, "note": ""}
        try:
            import io

            from PIL import Image

            image = Image.open(io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(payload)))
            image.load()
            width, height = image.size

            scale = min(1.0, MAX_VISION_IMAGE_SIDE / float(max(width, height) or 1))
            if scale < 1.0:
                image = image.resize(
                    (max(1, int(width * scale)), max(1, int(height * scale))),
                    Image.LANCZOS,
                )
            # JPEG has no alpha channel: flatten transparent screenshots.
            if image.mode not in ("RGB", "L"):
                image = image.convert("RGB")

            buffer = io.BytesIO()
            image.save(buffer, format="JPEG", quality=85, optimize=True)
            candidate = (
                "data:image/jpeg;base64,"
                + base64.b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode("ascii")
            )

            if len(candidate) < len(data_uri):
                result = {
                    "uri": candidate,
                    "note": (
                        f", downscaled {width}x{height} -> "
                        f"{image.size[0]}x{image.size[1]} (jpeg)"
                    ),
                }
                logger.info(
                    "Attachment '%s' downscaled %sx%s -> %sx%s "
                    "(%d -> %d base64 chars)",
                    file_name, width, height,
                    image.size[0], image.size[1],
                    len(payload), len(candidate),
                )
            else:
                result = {
                    "uri": data_uri,
                    "note": ", oversized (keeping original encoding)",
                }
                logger.warning(
                    "Attachment '%s' exceeds the vision payload budget and "
                    "re-encoding did not reduce it",
                    file_name,
                )
        except ImportError:
            result = {
                "uri": data_uri,
                "note": ", oversized (Pillow not available)",
            }
            logger.warning(
                "Attachment '%s' exceeds the vision payload budget and Pillow "
                "is not installed; sending it unchanged",
                file_name,
            )
        except (binascii.Error, ValueError, KeyError, OSError, Exception) as ex:
            result = {
                "uri": data_uri,
                "note": ", oversized (re-encode failed)",
            }
            logger.warning(
                "Attachment '%s' exceeds the vision payload budget and could "
                "not be re-encoded: %s",
                file_name, ex,
            )

        cls._cache_store(_IMAGE_SHRINK_CACHE, cache_key, result)
        return result["uri"], result["note"]

    @classmethod
    def _prepare_attachment(cls, item: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Resolve a single collected attachment into its outgoing representation.

        Normalizes the payload and decides whether it travels as an
        ``image_url`` content part or only as text. The returned dict is the
        single source of truth used by both
        :meth:`_build_attachment_parts` and
        :meth:`_build_attachment_text_block`.

        :param item: Attachment item from :meth:`collect_attachments`.
        :return: Dict with keys ``item``, ``file_name``, ``media_type``,
                 ``size_kb``, ``part`` (image part or None) and ``note``.
        """
        attachment = item["attachment"]
        media_type = cls._attachment_media_type(attachment)
        payload = cls._attachment_payload(attachment)
        file_name = (
            attachment.file_name
            if isinstance(attachment, ChatAttachment)
            else f"legacy attachment {item.get('label', '')}".strip()
        )

        prepared = {
            "item": item,
            "file_name": file_name,
            "media_type": media_type,
            "size_kb": round(len(payload) * 3 / 4 / 1024.0, 1),
            "part": None,
            "note": "",
        }

        if media_type not in VISION_IMAGE_MEDIA_TYPES:
            prepared["note"] = (
                f"not sent to the model ({media_type} is not a supported "
                f"vision format)"
            )
            return prepared

        if not payload:
            prepared["note"] = "not sent to the model (empty payload)"
            return prepared

        data_uri = f"data:{media_type};base64,{payload}"
        shrink_note = ""
        if len(data_uri) > MAX_VISION_IMAGE_CHARS:
            data_uri, shrink_note = cls._shrink_image_data_uri(
                data_uri=data_uri,
                payload=payload,
                file_name=file_name,
            )

        prepared["part"] = {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": data_uri}}
        prepared["note"] = f"sent to the model as image ({media_type}{shrink_note})"
        return prepared

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Attachment visibility
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def collect_attachments(self, chat, include_parent=True):
        """
        Collect every attachment the model must always see.

        Attachments of ALL visible messages are returned — parent chats first
        (grandparents first), then the current chat, in conversation order — so
        an image uploaded in an earlier turn keeps reaching the model on every
        following request instead of being lost with the text-only history
        rendering.

        Visibility rules:

        * current chat: ``hide`` / ``improvement`` messages are skipped,
        * parent chats: every VISIBLE message contributes (the ``is_answer``
          flag is not required — see
          :meth:`is_visible_parent_message`), and the traversal stops on
          ``ignore_parent_knowledge``,
        * duplicated payloads (same base64 data) are collapsed to one item.

        :param chat: The chat whose messages are inspected.
        :param include_parent: Whether parent chats contribute attachments.
        :return: List of ``{"role", "label", "attachment"}`` dicts in order.
        """
        items = []
        seen_payloads = set()

        if include_parent and chat.parent_id:
            self._collect_parent_attachments(
                chat=chat,
                items=items,
                seen_payloads=seen_payloads,
            )

        for index, message in enumerate(chat.messages):
            if message.hide or message.improvement:
                continue
            self._add_message_attachments(
                message=message,
                items=items,
                seen_payloads=seen_payloads,
                source="chat",
                index=index,
            )

        return items

    def _collect_parent_attachments(self, chat, items, seen_payloads):
        """
        Append the attachments of a chat's ancestor chain (grandparents first).

        Mirrors :meth:`build_parent_message_history`: stops on
        ``ignore_parent_knowledge`` and includes only VISIBLE messages (via
        :meth:`is_visible_parent_message`, i.e. no ``is_answer`` filtering), so
        attachments keep the same context as the rendered parent history.

        :param chat: The child chat whose ancestors are visited.
        :param items: Accumulator list of attachment items.
        :param seen_payloads: Set of already collected base64 payloads.
        """
        if not chat.parent_id or chat.ignore_parent_knowledge:
            return

        chat_manager = self._get_chat_manager(project_id=chat.owner_project_id)
        parent_chat = chat_manager.find_by_id(chat.parent_id)
        if not parent_chat:
            return

        self._collect_parent_attachments(
            chat=parent_chat,
            items=items,

    def _add_message_attachments(message, items, seen_payloads, source, index):
        """
        Append a single message's attachments to the collector.

        :param message: The message whose attachments are collected.
        :param items: Accumulator list of attachment items.
        :param seen_payloads: Set of already collected base64 payloads.
        :param source: Label prefix ("chat" or "parent").
        :param index: Message position inside its chat (used in the label).
        """
        role = message.role or "user"
        for attachment in (message.attachments or []):
            payload = (
                attachment.base64_data
                if isinstance(attachment, ChatAttachment)
                else str(attachment)
            )
            if payload in seen_payloads:
                continue
            seen_payloads.add(payload)
            items.append({

                "label": f"{source} turn {index + 1} · {role}",

        :return: Markdown block, or an empty string when there is nothing.

        for prepared in prepared_items:
            lines.append(
                f"- [{prepared['item']['label']}] {prepared['file_name']} "
                f"({prepared['media_type']}, {prepared['size_kb']} KB) — "
                f"{prepared['note']}"

        """
        Append a task-refinement prompt to the message list.

        Attachments are no longer copied here: they are collected from every
        visible message (including the current one) and appended to the request
        message by :meth:`build_ai_prompt_messages`.

        task_content = ""

        answer_messages = [
            message.content for message in chat.messages if message.is_answer

        if answer_messages:
            task_content += "Task Document Header:\n"
            task_content += concat_content(answer_messages)
            task_content += "\n\n"

        if parent_task:
            task_content += (
                f"\nYou are writing a child document.\n"
                f"This information comes from the parent document for your information:\n"
                f"<parent_document>\n{parent_task}\n</parent_document>\n"
            )

        if existing_document:
            task_content += (
                f"\n<document>\n{existing_document}\n</document>\n\n"
                f"<comments>\n{user_message.content}\n</comments>\n\n"
                f"INSTRUCTIONS:\n"
                f" * Read comments and update document content based on them\n"
                f" * Leave all parts of the document not affected by the comments untouched\n"
                f" * Output the final document content\n"
            )
        else:
            task_content += user_message.content

        refine_message = new_chat_message(role="user", content=task_content)
        messages.append(self.convert_message(refine_message))
        return messages

    def append_agent_message(self, chat, messages, user_message, iterations_left):
        """
        Append an agent-style prompt that instructs the model to complete a task.

        Attachments are no longer copied here: they are collected from every
        visible message (including the original one) and appended to the request
        message by :meth:`build_ai_prompt_messages`, so they stay visible across
        agent iterations.
        """
        parent_context = ""

        if not chat.ignore_parent_knowledge:
            parent_context = self._get_chat_analysis_parents(chat=chat)

        agent_content = (
            f"You are responsible to end this task.\n"
            f"Follow instructions and try to solve it with the minimum iterations needed.\n"
            f"<task>\n{chat.name}\n</task>\n\n"
        )

        if parent_context:
            agent_content += (
                f"You are writing a child document based on prior context:\n"
                f"<parent_context>\n{parent_context}\n</parent_context>\n\n"
            )

        agent_content += (
            f"<user_request>\n{user_message.content}\n</user_request>\n\n"
            f"You still have {iterations_left} attempts more to finish the task.\n"
            f"Return {AGENT_DONE_WORD} when the task is done.\n"
        )

        agent_message = new_chat_message(role="user", content=agent_content)
        messages.append(self.convert_message(agent_message))
        return messages

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Response parsing
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def extract_files_from_response(content):
        """
        Extract code blocks with filenames from the AI response content.
        """
        files = []
        lines = content.split("\n")
        i = 0

        while i < len(lines):
            line = lines[i]
            open_match = re.match(r'^```(\w+)\s+(.+)$', line)

            if open_match:
                language = open_match.group(1)
                file_path = open_match.group(2).strip()
                code_lines = []
                i += 1
                nesting_depth = 1

                while i < len(lines) and nesting_depth > 0:
                    current_line = lines[i]

                    if re.match(r'^```(\w+)', current_line):
                        nesting_depth += 1
                        code_lines.append(current_line)
                    elif current_line == '```':
                        nesting_depth -= 1
                        if nesting_depth > 0:
                            code_lines.append(current_line)
                    else:
                        code_lines.append(current_line)

                    i += 1

                if file_path:
                    files.append({
                        "language": language,
                        "file_path": file_path,
                        "content": "\n".join(code_lines),
                    })
            else:
                i += 1

        logger.info("Extracted %d files from response content", len(files))
        return files

        :param message: The message to append.
        """
        if any(m.doc_id == message.doc_id for m in chat.messages):
            logger.debug(
                "Message '%s' already present in chat '%s', skipping append",
                message.doc_id,
                chat.doc_id,
            )
            return
        chat.messages.append(message)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: resolve chat mode flags
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _resolve_chat_mode_flags(
        self,
        chat: Chat,
        chat_mode: Optional[str],
        task_item: Optional[str]
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Resolve boolean flags that drive branching logic from the chat mode and task item.

        :param chat: The current chat object.
        :param chat_mode: Explicit mode override (may be None).
        :param task_item: Task item from the latest user message.
        :return: Dict with keys: chat_mode, is_refine, is_agent, is_vibe,
                 is_search, needs_pre_search.
        """
        resolved_mode = chat_mode or chat.mode or "chat"
        is_refine: bool = _is_refine(resolved_mode)
        is_agent: bool = resolved_mode == CHAT_MODE_AGENT
        is_vibe: bool = resolved_mode == CHAT_MODE_VIBE
        is_search: bool = task_item == TASK_ITEM_SEARCH
        needs_pre_search: bool = False # Deprecatred, use tools

        logger.info(
            "Resolved chat mode flags: mode=%s is_refine=%s is_agent=%s "
            "is_vibe=%s is_search=%s needs_pre_search=%s",
            resolved_mode, is_refine, is_agent, is_vibe, is_search, needs_pre_search
        )

        return {
            "chat_mode": resolved_mode,
            "is_refine": is_refine,
            "is_agent": is_agent,
            "is_vibe": is_vibe,
            "is_search": is_search,
            "needs_pre_search": needs_pre_search,
        }

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: collect all files referenced across visible messages
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _collect_files_from_visible_messages(
        valid_messages: List[Message],
        chat_base_files: List[str]
    ) -> List[str]:
        """
        Collect and deduplicate all file references from visible (non-hidden,
        non-improvement) messages plus the chat-level base file list.

        This ensures that files attached to *any* prior message are included in
        the working context, not just those on the most recent user message.

        flowchart TD
            A[chat.file_list] --> D[Union]
            B[Each visible message .files] --> D
            C[Deduplicate] --> E[Sorted list]
            D --> C

        :param valid_messages: All non-hidden, non-improvement messages for the turn.
        :param chat_base_files: Files already present on ``chat.file_list``.
        :return: Deduplicated, sorted list of file paths.
        """
        all_files: Set[str] = set(chat_base_files)
        for message in valid_messages:
            if message.files:
                all_files.update(message.files)
        # Sort for deterministic ordering
        return sorted(all_files)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: resolve linked (nested) profiles (ADDED)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _resolve_linked_profiles(self, profiles: List[Profile]) -> List[Profile]:
        """
        Expand a list of profiles with the profiles they link to.

        Each :class:`Profile` may reference other profiles by name in its
        ``profiles`` property. Linked profiles can themselves link to more
        profiles, so the graph is expanded **recursively** and deduplicated
        (first occurrence wins, order preserved).

        This guarantees that the content, tools and agents (profile names) of
        every linked profile participate when processing a chat. Resolution is
        delegated to :class:`ProfileManager` (the same logic used for file
        profiles) and is best-effort: on failure the original list is returned
        so a chat is never blocked by a profile-resolution error.

        :param profiles: Profiles referenced directly by the chat/mentions.
        :return: The input profiles plus all their (recursively) linked profiles.
        """
        if not profiles:
            return profiles
        try:
            resolved = self.get_profile_manager().reduce_linked_profiles(
                profiles=profiles
            )
            logger.info(
                "Resolved %d profile(s) to %d after expanding linked profiles: %s",
                len(profiles),
                len(resolved),
                [p.name for p in resolved],
            )
            return resolved
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.exception(
                "Failed to resolve linked profiles, using %d base profile(s): %s",
                len(profiles),
                ex,
            )
            return profiles

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: build the TEAM section of the system prompt (ADDED)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _build_team_system_section(team_profiles: List[Profile]) -> str:
        """
        Render the TEAM section appended AFTER the profile composition.

        ``team`` is a profile property listing profile NAMES the model can use
        in NEW tasks (like ``profiles`` lists linked profiles). Team members are
        NOT active in this turn: their content, tools and model are not applied,
        they are only offered as a table (name + short description) so the model
        knows who can take what kind of work and can hand it off instead of
        impersonating them.

        flowchart TD
            A[Active profiles .team] --> B[ProfileManager.get_team_profiles]
            B --> C{Any member?}
            C -->|No| D[No section]
            C -->|Yes| E[Markdown table: profile | description]
            E --> F[Appended after the profile composition]

        :param team_profiles: Resolved team profiles (see
                              :meth:`ProfileManager.get_team_profiles`).
        :return: Markdown section, or an empty string when there is no team.
        """
        if not team_profiles:
            return ""

        lines = [
            "### TEAM",
            "Profiles you can use in NEW tasks. They are NOT active in this turn: "
            "never answer on their behalf. When a request belongs to one of them, "
            "say so and ask the user to run that task with the profile "
            "(@profile_name).",
            "",
            "| Profile | Description |",
            "| --- | --- |",
        ]
        for profile in team_profiles:
            description = ProfileManager.profile_short_description(profile=profile)
            # Keep the table well formed.
            description = description.replace("|", "\\|")
            lines.append(f"| `{profile.name}` | {description} |")
        return "\n".join(lines)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: resolve profiles, model and tools
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _resolve_profiles_and_model(
        self,
        chat: Chat,
        query_mentions: QueryMentions,
        chat_files: List[str],
        is_refine: bool
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Derive the active profiles, LLM model, tool list, and profile content string
        from the query mentions and chat state.

        CHANGED: the mentioned profiles are first expanded with their **linked
        profiles** (the ``profiles`` property, recursively) so that the content,
        tools and agents of every linked profile are applied to the process.

        ADDED — team: after the profile composition a ``### TEAM`` section is
        appended with the profiles the model can use in NEW tasks (the ``team``
        property of the active profiles). Team members are neither composed into
        the prompt nor activated: they only appear as a name/description table,
        resolved by :meth:`ProfileManager.get_team_profiles`. Profiles already
        active in the turn are not offered again.

        Profiles are sorted by name and their content is formatted to be passed
        as part of the AI system prompt, including the current date/time.

        flowchart TD
            A[Query mentions profiles] --> A1[Expand linked profiles - recursive]
            A1 --> A2[Resolve team profiles - not composed]
            A2 --> B{Any profiles?}
            B -->|Yes| C[Sort profiles by name]
            C --> D[Build system prompt content]
            D --> D1[Append TEAM table after the composition]
            D1 --> E[Collect tools from all profiles]
            E --> F{Profile has model?}
            F -->|Yes| G[Set chat_model from profile]
            F -->|No| H[Keep existing model]
            B -->|No| I{Any chat_files?}
            I -->|Yes| J[Set default profile content]
            I -->|No| K[Empty profile content]

        :param chat: The current chat object.
        :param query_mentions: Resolved mentions from the user query.
        :param chat_files: List of files attached to the chat.
        :param is_refine: Whether we are in task/refine mode.
        :return: Dict with keys: chat_profiles_system_content, chat_profile_names,
                 chat_team_names, chat_model, chat_tools, is_refine.
        """
        # Resolve nested/linked profiles: each profile may reference other
        # profiles by name through its ``profiles`` property. Expand recursively
        # and deduplicate so every linked profile — with its content, tools and
        # agents — participates in the process.
        all_profiles = self._resolve_linked_profiles(query_mentions.profiles)
        chat_profiles_system_content = ""
        chat_profile_names: List[str] = []
        chat_team_names: List[str] = []
        chat_model: Optional[str] = chat.llm_model
        chat_tools: List[str] = []

        if all_profiles:
            # Sort profiles by name for consistent ordering
            sorted_profiles = sorted(all_profiles, key=lambda p: p.name)
            
            profile_blocks = []
            for profile in sorted_profiles:
                block = f"### PROFILE: {profile.name}\n"
                block += profile.parsed_content
                profile_blocks.append(block)
            
            chat_profiles_system_content = "\n\n".join(profile_blocks)
            chat_profile_names = [profile.name for profile in sorted_profiles]

            # ADDED: TEAM section — the profiles the model can use in NEW tasks.
            # Appended AFTER the profile composition and built only from the
            # ``team`` property of the active profiles. Team members are NOT
            # composed into the prompt and are NOT activated (their content,
            # tools and model do not apply to this turn), and the profiles
            # already active are excluded (they are being used right now).
            chat_team_profiles = self.get_profile_manager().get_team_profiles(
                profiles=sorted_profiles,
                exclude=sorted_profiles,
            )
            team_system_section = self._build_team_system_section(
                team_profiles=chat_team_profiles
            )
            if team_system_section:
                chat_profiles_system_content = concat_content([
                    chat_profiles_system_content,
                    team_system_section,
                ])
                chat_team_names = [p.name for p in chat_team_profiles]
                logger.info(
                    "Team profiles offered for new tasks: %s", chat_team_names
                )

            for profile in sorted_profiles:
                chat_tools = chat_tools + profile.tools
                logger.info("Profile '%s (%s)' tools: '%s'", profile.name, profile.project_id, profile.tools)
            chat_tools = list(set(chat_tools))
            

            if not chat_model:
                profile_models = [p for p in sorted_profiles if p.llm_model]
                if profile_models:
                    profile_model = profile_models[0]
                    chat_model = profile_model.llm_model
                    logger.info(
                        "chat_model '%s' from profile: '%s'",
                        profile_model.llm_model,
                        profile_model.name
                    )

            if next((p for p in sorted_profiles if _is_refine(p.chat_mode)), None):
                is_refine = True

        elif chat_files:
            chat_profiles_system_content = (
                "Focus on the changes required by the task "
                "and keep all other content as it is."
            )

        return {
            "chat_profiles_system_content": chat_profiles_system_content,
            "chat_profile_names": chat_profile_names,
            "chat_team_names": chat_team_names,
            "chat_model": chat_model,
            "chat_tools": chat_tools,
            "is_refine": is_refine,
        }

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: resolve guardrail service for all active profiles (UPDATED)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _resolve_guardrail_service(self, query_mentions: QueryMentions):
        """
        Return a GuardrailService aggregating the guardrail policies of every
        profile active in the current turn.

        Each profile now carries its own ``guardrails`` policy (not tied to
        ``api_settings``). When several profiles work together in one chat,
        their policies are combined so input, output and tool checks are
        enforced for all of them.

        :param query_mentions: Resolved mentions for the current user query.
        :return: GuardrailService instance or None when no profile enables guardrails.
        """
        profiles = [
            p for p in query_mentions.profiles
            if p.guardrails and p.guardrails.enabled
        ]
        if not profiles:
            return None

        from codx.junior.guardrails.service import GuardrailService

        return GuardrailService(
            policies=[p.guardrails for p in profiles],
            settings=self.settings,
        )

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: evaluate knowledge-disable conditions
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _evaluate_knowledge_flags(
        self,
        chat: Chat,
        disable_knowledge: bool,
        search_projects: List[CODXJuniorSettings],
        user_message: Message
    ) -> bool:
        """
        Determine whether knowledge search should be disabled, emitting events as needed.

        :param chat: The current chat object.
        :param disable_knowledge: Incoming disable flag.
        :param search_projects: Resolved search projects.
        :param user_message: The latest user message.
        :return: True if knowledge should be disabled, False otherwise.
        """
        if disable_knowledge:
            self.event_manager.chat_event(
                chat=chat,
                message="Knowledge search is disabled: Disabled by invocation"
            )
            return True

        if not search_projects:
            self.event_manager.chat_event(
                chat=chat,
                message="Knowledge search is disabled: No search projects found"
            )
            return True

        if not self.settings.use_knowledge:
            self.event_manager.chat_event(
                chat=chat,
                message="Knowledge search is disabled: Project settings disabled"
            )
            return True

        if user_message.disable_knowledge:
            self.event_manager.chat_event(
                chat=chat,
                message="Knowledge search is disabled: Disabled by user message"
            )
            return True

        return False

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: detect if a file is binary
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _is_binary_file(file_path: str) -> bool:
        """
        Determine if a file is binary based on its extension.

        :param file_path: Path to the file.
        :return: True if file appears to be binary, False otherwise.
        """
        _, ext = os.path.splitext(file_path)
        ext = ext.lstrip(".").lower()
        
        binary_extensions = {
            "pdf", "png", "jpg", "jpeg", "gif", "webp", "bmp", "svg",
            "ico", "tiff", "zip", "tar", "gz", "7z", "rar", "exe",
            "dll", "so", "pyc", "o", "a", "lib"
        }
        
        return ext in binary_extensions

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: load content for explicitly attached chat files
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _load_chat_files_content(
        self,
        chat_files: List[str],
        already_in_messages: Set[str],
        file_base_paths: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None
    ) -> Tuple[str, List[Dict[str, str]]]:
        """
        Read and format the content of files explicitly attached to the chat.

        Separates text and binary files:
        - Text files: returned as formatted code blocks in the content string
        - Binary files (PDFs, images): returned as separate list for vision API

        Files already embedded as code blocks in the message history are skipped
        to avoid duplication.

        ADDED: Chat file references may be RELATIVE and are relative to the
        project that owns the chat (``project_id`` if present, otherwise
        ``owner_project_id``) — NOT necessarily the current engine settings.
        ``file_base_paths`` maps each file path to the project root it must be
        resolved against; files missing from the map fall back to the current
        engine project path.

        ADDED: files attached to a message that declares its own ``project_id``
        map to THAT project's root, so a single chat can work on files living
        in another project (see :meth:`_resolve_message_project_path`).

        CHANGED: Now returns a tuple of (text_content, binary_files_list).
        Binary files are detected and separated for potential vision API processing.

        :param chat_files: List of file paths to load.
        :param already_in_messages: Set of file paths already present in message bodies.
        :param file_base_paths: Optional mapping of file path -> project root path
                                used to resolve relative file references.
        :return: Tuple of (formatted_text_content_string, binary_files_list).
        """
        chat_files_content = ""
        binary_files = []
        file_base_paths = file_base_paths or {}
        
        for chat_file in chat_files:
            if chat_file in already_in_messages:
                continue

            # Resolve against the owning chat's project (parent files can live
            # in a different project than the current engine settings).
            base_project_path = (
                file_base_paths.get(chat_file) or self.settings.abs_project_path
            )

            chat_file_full_path = self._resolve_chat_file_path(
                chat_file=chat_file,
                base_project_path=base_project_path
            )
            if not chat_file_full_path:
                continue

            try:
                # Check if binary BEFORE attempting to read as text
                if self._is_binary_file(chat_file_full_path):
                    logger.info(
                        "Binary file detected (will pass to LLM separately): '%s'",
                        chat_file_full_path
                    )
                    binary_files.append({
                        "path": chat_file,
                        "full_path": chat_file_full_path
                    })
                    continue
                
                with open(chat_file_full_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                    source = chat_file_full_path.replace(
                        base_project_path + "/", ""
                    )
                    logger.info(
                        "Loading chat_file content from '%s' with source: '%s'",
                        chat_file_full_path,
                        source
                    )
                    doc_context = self._document_to_context(
                        Document(
                            page_content=fh.read(),
                            metadata={"source": source}
                        )
                    )
                    chat_files_content += doc_context + "\n"
            except UnicodeDecodeError:
                logger.warning(
                    "Failed to decode '%s' as UTF-8; treating as binary",
                    chat_file_full_path
                )
                binary_files.append({
                    "path": chat_file,
                    "full_path": chat_file_full_path
                })
            except OSError as ex:
                logger.error("Error adding context file to chat: %s", ex)

        return chat_files_content, binary_files

    def _document_to_context(self, doc: Document) -> str:
        """
        Convert a Document to a formatted context string with language-specific code fence.

        :param doc: The Document to convert.
        :return: Formatted context string with file metadata and code fence.
        """
        content = doc.page_content
        source = doc.metadata['source']
        language = doc.metadata.get('language')
        extension = source.split(".")[-1] if "." in source else ""

        language = language or extension
        language = LANGUAGE_PARSER_MAPPING.get(language, language)
        
        return concat_content([
            "### FILE CONTEXT",
            f"This is the actual project's file content for '{source}', use same file path in your response.",
            "This content represent the current file, use it as a base for changes.",
            "",
            f"```{language} {source}",
            content,
            "```",
            ""
        ])

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: resolve a project id to its absolute project path
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _resolve_project_path(self, project_id: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        Resolve a project id to the absolute path of its project.

        Uses the current engine settings when they already match *project_id*
        (fast path) and falls back to project discovery otherwise.

        :param project_id: The project id to resolve (may be None).
        :return: The absolute project path, or None when it cannot be resolved.
        """
        if not project_id:
            return None
        # Fast path: the engine is already scoped to this project.
        if project_id == self.settings.project_id:
            return self.settings.abs_project_path
        project_settings = find_project_by_id(project_id=project_id)
        if project_settings and project_settings.abs_project_path:
            return project_settings.abs_project_path
        return None

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: resolve the project path a chat's files are relative to
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _resolve_chat_project_path(self, chat: Chat) -> str:
        """
        Resolve the absolute project path that a chat's file references are
        relative to.

        Chat file lists (``chat.file_list``) and message attachments may store
        *relative* paths. Those paths are relative to the chat's working
        project: ``project_id`` when present, otherwise ``owner_project_id``.

        This matters especially for parent chats, which can live in a different
        project than the current engine settings.

        :param chat: The chat whose project base path to resolve (may be None).
        :return: Absolute project path used as the base for the chat's files.
        """
        if chat:
            for project_id in (chat.project_id, chat.owner_project_id):
                project_path = self._resolve_project_path(project_id=project_id)
                if project_path:
                    return project_path
        return self.settings.abs_project_path

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: resolve the project the CURRENT turn works on (ADDED)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _resolve_turn_project_id(chat: Chat) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        Resolve the project the CURRENT turn works on.

        The user message of the turn may declare its own ``project_id`` (like a
        :class:`Chat` does). When set, that project becomes the MAIN project of
        the turn: it takes precedence over ``chat.project_id``, the engine
        switches its context to it and every file of the turn is resolved
        against it.

        ``owner_project_id`` is NOT a working project — it only tells where the
        chat is persisted — so it is never used here.

        flowchart TD
            A[Last visible user message] --> B{project_id set?}
            B -->|Yes| C[Main project = message.project_id]
            B -->|No| D[Main project = chat.project_id]
            D --> E{defined?}
            E -->|No| F[None - engine project is used]

        :param chat: The chat being processed.
        :return: The project id the turn works on, or None when unknown.
        """
        for message in reversed(chat.messages or []):
            if message.hide or message.improvement or message.role != "user":
                continue
            if message.project_id:
                return message.project_id
            # Only the CURRENT request defines the turn scope: previous user
            # messages must not leak their project into this turn.
            break
        return chat.project_id or None

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: resolve the project path a MESSAGE's files are relative to (ADDED)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _resolve_message_project_path(
        self,
        message: Optional[Message],
        chat: Optional[Chat]
    ) -> str:
        """
        Resolve the absolute project path that a message's file references are
        relative to.

        A message may declare its own ``project_id`` (like a ``Chat`` does), so
        a single chat can work on files that live in another project. When the
        message does not define one — or it points to an unknown project — the
        chat's project path is used.

        The engine project is NOT switched here: the chat (and therefore its
        persistence) still belongs to its own project. Only the file resolution
        of the message is affected.

        flowchart TD
            A[message.project_id] --> B{defined?}
            B -->|No| C[chat project path]
            B -->|Yes| D[resolve project path]
            D -->|found| E[message project path]
            D -->|not found| F[log warning + chat project path]

        :param message: The message whose project to resolve (may be None).
        :param chat: The chat that owns the message (may be None).
        :return: Absolute project path used as the base for the message's files.
        """
        message_project_path = self._resolve_project_path(
            project_id=message.project_id if message else None
        )
        if message_project_path:
            return message_project_path

        chat_project_path = self._resolve_chat_project_path(chat=chat)
        if message and message.project_id:
            logger.warning(
                "Message '%s' declares unknown project_id '%s'; falling back to "
                "the chat project path '%s'",
                message.doc_id,
                message.project_id,
                chat_project_path,
            )
        return chat_project_path

    def _resolve_chat_file_path(
        self,
        chat_file: str,
        base_project_path: Optional[str] = None
    ) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        Resolve the full filesystem path of a chat-attached file.

        Files may be absolute or relative. Relative paths are resolved against
        *base_project_path* — the project that owns the chat the file belongs
        to — falling back to the current engine project when not provided.

        Returns None and logs a warning if the file cannot be found.

        :param chat_file: Relative or absolute file path.
        :param base_project_path: Project root the relative path is based on.
        :return: Resolved absolute path, or None if unresolvable.
        """
        base_project_path = base_project_path or self.settings.abs_project_path

        if chat_file.startswith(base_project_path) or os.path.isfile(chat_file):
            return chat_file

        logger.info(
            "Normalizing chat_file '%s' for project path: '%s'",
            chat_file,
            base_project_path
        )
        normalized = chat_file.lstrip("/")
        full_path = os.path.join(base_project_path, normalized)
        return full_path

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: convert binary files to vision API format
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _prepare_vision_content(
        binary_files: List[Dict[str, str]]
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Convert binary files to OpenAI vision API format.

        Supports image files only. Image files are converted to base64-encoded
        data URIs in the image_url format supported by OpenAI's vision API.

        PDF support is not included as OpenAI's API does not accept PDFs in the
        image_url or file format via data URIs.

        Format returned matches OpenAI Chat Completions API vision support:
        https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/vision

        CHANGED: Simplified to only handle image files. PDFs are skipped with
        a debug log. Message attachments are NOT processed here: they are
        gathered from every visible message by
        :meth:`ChatPromptBuilder.collect_attachments` and appended to the
        request message by :meth:`ChatPromptBuilder.build_ai_prompt_messages`.

        :param binary_files: List of {'path', 'full_path'} dicts from chat files.
        :return: List of content blocks (image_url type only).
        """
        vision_content = []

        for binary_file in binary_files:
            full_path = binary_file["full_path"]
            mime_type = ChatEngine._get_mime_type_for_file(full_path)
            
            # Only process image files; skip PDFs and unsupported types
            if not mime_type.startswith("image/"):
                logger.debug(
                    "Skipping non-image file for vision API: %s (mime_type=%s)",
                    full_path, mime_type
                )
                continue
            
            try:
                with open(full_path, "rb") as f:
                    file_bytes = f.read()
                base64_data = base64.b64encode(file_bytes).decode("utf-8")
                
                # Format as data URI (supported by vision models)
                data_uri = f"data:{mime_type};base64,{base64_data}"
                
                vision_content.append({
                    "type": "image_url",
                    "image_url": {"url": data_uri}
                })
                logger.info(
                    "Added image file to vision content: %s",
                    full_path
                )
            except OSError as ex:
                logger.warning("Failed to read binary file %s: %s", full_path, ex)

        return vision_content

    @staticmethod
    def _get_mime_type_for_file(file_path: str) -> str:
        """
        Determine MIME type from file extension.

        :param file_path: File path.
        :return: MIME type string.
        """
        _, ext = os.path.splitext(file_path)
        ext = ext.lstrip(".").lower()
        
        mime_map = {
            "pdf": "application/pdf",
            "png": "image/png",
            "jpg": "image/jpeg",
            "jpeg": "image/jpeg",
            "gif": "image/gif",
            "webp": "image/webp",
        }
        
        return mime_map.get(ext, "application/octet-stream")

    async def _run_pre_search(
        self,
        chat: Chat,
        messages: List,
        query: str,
        chat_files: List[str]
    ) -> Tuple[List[Document], List[str], str]:
        """
        Execute the AI-driven pre-search used in vibe and search modes.

        Combines conversation history with the current query to build a richer
        search query, then delegates to ChatKnowledge.

        :param chat: The current chat object.
        :param messages: Existing LangChain messages (history).
        :param query: The raw user query string.
        :param chat_files: Files already attached to the chat.
        :return: Tuple of (documents, file_list, context_string).
        """
        history_context = concat_content([m.content for m in messages])
        pre_search_query = f"{history_context}\n{query}".strip()

        pre_docs, pre_file_list, pre_context = (
            await self.chat_knowledge.ai_search_for_context(
                chat=chat,
                query=pre_search_query,
                existing_chat_files=chat_files
            )
        )
        logger.info("Pre-search added %d documents to context", len(pre_docs))
        return pre_docs, pre_file_list, pre_context

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helper: standard RAG knowledge search
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _run_rag_knowledge_search(
        self,
        chat: Chat,
        messages: List,
        query: str,
        ignore_documents: List[str],
        search_projects: List[CODXJuniorSettings]
    ) -> Tuple[List[Document], List[str], str]:
        """
        Perform the standard RAG document search across the given search projects.

        :param chat: The current chat object.
        :param messages: Existing LangChain message history.
        :param query: The raw user query string.
        :param ignore_documents: File paths to exclude from search results.
        :param search_projects: Projects to search within.
        :return: Tuple of (documents, file_list, context_string).
        """
        rag_documents: List[Document] = []
        file_list: List[str] = []
        context = ""

        chat.messages.append(
            self._new_chat_message(
                "assistant",
                content=f"Searching in {[p.project_name for p in search_projects]}"
            )
        )
        logger.info("chat_with_project start project search %s", search_projects)

        try:
            if query:
                query_context = concat_content([message.content for message in messages])
                search_query = self.chat_knowledge.create_knowledge_search_query(
                    query=f"{query_context}\n{query}"
                )
                self.event_manager.chat_event(
                    chat=chat,
                    message=f"Knowledge searching for: {search_query}"
                )

                rag_documents, file_list = (
                    self.chat_knowledge.select_documents_from_knowledge(
                        chat=chat,
                        query=search_query,
                        ignore_documents=ignore_documents,
                        search_projects=search_projects
                    )
                )
                for doc in rag_documents:
                    doc_context = document_to_code_block(doc)
                    context += f"{doc_context}\n"

            self.event_manager.chat_event(
                chat=chat,
                message=f"Knowledge search found {len(rag_documents)} relevant documents"
            )
        except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as ex:
            self.event_manager.chat_event(
                chat=chat,
                message=f"!!Error searching in knowledge {ex}",
                event_type="error"
            )
            logger.exception("!!Error searching in knowledge: %s", ex)

        return rag_documents, file_list, context
